title: fix(app-shell,i18n): tell an override reassign what a reassign does (objectui#13164)
body:
Fixes #13164

Clause-②: yes

## What was wrong

On Setup → Approvals, an admin who holds no approver slot and clicks **Override Reassign** was shown the decision sentence: "Continuing uses your admin override: it finalises the step immediately and bypasses the approvers who have not acted — NAMES. The decision is recorded as an admin override." A reassign finalises nothing. `DeclaredActionsBar` composed `overrideNotice` from two facts only: is this an override, and can the bypassed approvers be named. `isOverrideDecision` admits every lever whose declared `visible` ORs in `can_override`, so approve, reject and reassign all got the same sentence.

## What an override reassign does (measured on the server, not assumed)

Read in `ApprovalService.reassign` (`plugin-approvals`) at objectui's pinned objectstack SHA (`.objectstack-sha`, `f4755a68a`). The function is byte-identical on objectstack `main` today.

- The console's reassign sends `to` and `comment`, never `from`, so `from` falls back to the caller. A caller with no slot (`takenSlot` answers nothing; it is the same `heldSlot` test `viewer.can_act` is computed from) takes the admin-rescue branch, which sets the slate to the chosen person alone (`next = [to]`). Every approver still pending on the step is replaced.
- The request's `status` is not written. It stays `pending` and now waits on the new approver. The card measured the same thing: "the request stayed Pending, and now waits on the new assignee".
- The `reassign` action row is written with `via_override: true` (`isOverride && slot === undefined`), and the new approver is notified.

## The change

- `DeclaredActionsBar.tsx`: a module-level `approvalRouteVerb(action)` reads which approvals lever a declared action pulls from its `target` route (`/approve`, `/reject`, `/reassign`). It replaces the two inline regexes the click handler used to pick the decision for the decision-output params, with the same answer for every route. The notice now asks it too. A reassign override gets its own sentence, and every other override lever keeps today's sentence. There is no action-name list.
- New copy (en): "You hold no approver slot on this step. Continuing uses your admin override: the step moves to the new approver you pick, replacing the approvers who have not acted — NAMES. The request stays pending and waits on the new approver. The reassignment is recorded as an admin override." There is also an unnamed form ("… replacing any approver who has not acted. …") for an empty slate.
- `approvalsInbox.overrideReassignNotice` and `approvalsInbox.overrideReassignNoticeWho` are added to all ten packs. They are translations, not English copies, and each one reuses its pack's existing words for the override, the new approver and "pending".
- Unchanged: the approve and reject override sentences (named and unnamed), `overrideActionLabel`, the no-notice path for a slot holder, and the request that is sent.
- Changeset: `@object-ui/app-shell` patch, `@object-ui/i18n` patch.

`Clause-②: yes`: the two new keys widen `@object-ui/i18n`'s exported `TranslationKeys`. Nothing narrows.

## Tests

There is a new `describe` in `DeclaredActionsBar.overrideAffordance.test.tsx`:

- The reassign override's notice equals the en pack's `overrideReassignNoticeWho` with the names filled in, and it contains no "finalis".
- The unnamed form equals `overrideReassignNotice`.
- Controls: the approve and reject notices equal today's `overrideNoticeWho` and `overrideNotice`.
- The label stays "Override Reassign".
- A slot holder gets no notice.
- The reassign dispatch carries only its own params (`to`, `comment`), even when the row declares decision outputs.

The expected sentences are read from the en pack instead of being typed again in the test. `pnpm check:i18n-keys` keeps each inline `defaultValue` equal to its pack value.

**Ablation.** The fix was committed first. Then the producer was reverted to BASE `3cec0901f` with a whole-file `git show`. The on-disk hash was checked against BASE's blob, and the marker counts moved from 2 to 0 (`overrideReassignNotice`) and from 4 to 0 (`approvalRouteVerb`). The restore ran under a trap through `git checkout HEAD --`. It was confirmed by the on-disk hash matching the HEAD blob and by an empty `git diff HEAD`.

- Ablated: `Tests  2 failed | 22 passed (24)`. The two failures are exactly the two reassign-notice tests. The ablated "Received" is the card's Actual word for word: "… it finalises the step immediately and bypasses the approvers who have not acted — Qian Hua, Li Lei. The decision is recorded as an admin override."
- Restored: green (see below). The test file loads the bar and the i18n pack from source (a relative import and the vitest alias), so no `dist` sits between the mutation and the run.

## Acceptance notes

- **Outside this card: an override Recall gets the same decision sentence.** At the pinned SHA, `plugin-approvals` declares `approval_recall` with a `can_override` arm (objectstack#12716), so `isOverrideDecision` admits it. I ran a throwaway unit probe (not committed) with recall declared as shipped. For an override-only admin, and also for a submitter who is an admin (`can_act: false`, `is_submitter: true`, `can_override: true`), the button reads "Override Recall" and the notice says "it finalises the step immediately and bypasses the approvers who have not acted — Qian Hua. The decision is recorded as an admin override." On the server, `ApprovalService.recall` withdraws the request (`status: 'recalled'`) and writes its `recall` action row with no `via_override`. So "recorded as an admin override" is not what happens, and a submitter recalling their own request is told it is an override. The header of `utils/approvalOverride.ts` ("`approval_recall` / `approval_resubmit` gate on `is_submitter` and never match") and this suite's `approval_recall` fixture (submitter-only `visible`) both describe the declaration as it was before objectstack#12716. This PR leaves recall's text exactly as it was, because the admission rule is outside this card's scope. The report hands the finding to the seat.
- The zh pack's two existing override sentences use ASCII `:` and `,` where the rest of the pack uses full-width punctuation. The new zh sentences use full-width punctuation. This is typography only, and no card was filed.
